name: documented-store
description: Two entities carrying every facet the generated OpenAPI document has to publish, and exactly one facet per reason: a declared field description, an enum, a maxLength, a built-in format, a descriptor-declared format (so a published 'pattern' is distinguishable from a published 'format'), a decimal whose precision/scale JSON Schema cannot express, a date and a datetime (the two wire encodings a type alone does not imply), a json field (whose request and response shapes genuinely differ), a nullable field (the sort key a paged read refuses), a readOnly field, an optional hidden field WITH its own description (so 'excluded from every schema' covers the prose as well as the name), a required-AND-hidden field (a mandatory secret a caller must supply on create but can never read back — the one case a hidden field's name is published, and only in the write schemas), and a required ref. 'products' is audited and 'categories' is not, which is what makes '304 and ETag are documented only where a row has a version' a claim two entities can disagree about — a one-entity descriptor would let that pass whichever way the code went.

sku-code.description: Three upper-case letters, a dash, four digits. Deliberately written without anchors, so the published pattern shows the anchoring the API applies rather than the author's.

categories.description: A product category. Not audited, so its rows carry no version — no ETag is minted for them and no conditional read or write of one is possible.

code.description: An optional short code, unique across categories. Declared so a 409 on this entity's update is reachable — a duplicate on a field declared unique is the only way a PATCH reaches one, and every documented status has to be reachable.

products.description: A product in the catalogue. Audited, so every row carries a version and every read and write of one can be made conditional.

name.description: The product's display name, as it appears on an invoice.

sku.description: The stock-keeping unit, unique across the catalogue.

contact.description: Who to ask about this product.

status.description: Where the product is in its life cycle.

released_on.description: The day the product went on sale.

discontinued_at.description: When the product was withdrawn, if it has been.

in_stock.description: Whether any unit is currently on hand.

specs.description: Whatever the supplier publishes about the product.

slug.description: The URL segment this product is published under. Maintained outside the API.

cost.description: What the product costs us. Commercially confidential: neither the value nor the fact that this field exists may reach a caller.

activation_secret.description: A one-time activation token the caller must supply on create and can never read back.

category_id.description: The category this product belongs to.

parent_id.description: An optional parent product. A self-reference, and the cheapest way to make a 409 on THIS entity's delete reachable: 'categories' is already made conflict-on-delete by 'category_id' above, and a third entity would only move the problem to whatever nothing references.
